periods.time: During the Kyushu Daien crisis, before the planned討伐

name.zh: 美国太平洋舰队侵入日本专属经济海域
name.en: U.S. Pacific Fleet invades Japan's EEZ

periods.location: Pacific Ocean east of Japan; League Japan Branch command room
periods.summary: Douglas Upton leads the U.S. Pacific Fleet toward Japan, ignores Self-Defense warnings, claims that PSYON captured Prime Minister Bakuya Tsukikage at a Rebellion base, and declares that the Union will punish Japan and the League for allegedly controlling Rebellion. Upton destroys a Japanese aircraft with a giant sea-water hand and threatens indiscriminate bombing of Tokyo. Itsuki Kurogane declares a national emergency, activates the Integrated Operations Center, and orders all forces to engage.
periods.cause: The United States and Union use Tsukikage's alleged confession as a pretext to force Japan's disarmament and shift the world order.
periods.process: Japanese Self-Defense aircraft warn the fleet. Upton openly refuses to turn back and frames the attack as justice. In Tokyo, Itsuki concludes the accusation is one-sided and likely strategic, then uses emergency authority because Tsukikage is absent.
periods.outcome: Japan enters wartime emergency. Tokyo's defenses, shelters, self-defense forces, and student knight conscription activate. The Kyushu Daien operation is jeopardized because Kurono is needed in the capital.
periods.significance: Opens the second battlefield of the volume and forces Japan to choose between Kyushu and Tokyo priorities.
